notes: §1985:XIV.3.2.4 GR4 (as amended by X3.23a-1989): DISABLE INPUT TERMINAL deactivates "the logical paths between the source (as defined by the content of the data item referenced by data-name-7 (SYMBOLIC SOURCE)) and all of its associated queues and sub-queues". SetPath's InputTerminal arm disables the SourceEndpoint named at positions 63-74 (21 when unknown or blank, 15 when already disabled), and MessageStoreState#Deliver holds every destination whose source is disabled, whatever queue level it feeds, releasing them on ENABLE. Probes at --std 85: a blank source 21; unknown TX 21; T1 held out of Q1/S1/S2 while T2 delivered (count 1, then 2 after ENABLE); a repeat 15; a wrong KEY 40. The witness checks two queues of one source and a second source.

next.reason: Amendment X3.23a-1989 only closed a parenthesis ('SOURCE)' to 'SOURCE))'): 'the logical paths between the source (as defined by the content of the data item referenced by data-name-7 (SYMBOLIC SOURCE)) and all of its associated queues and sub-queues are deactivated' (§1985:XIV.3.2.4 GR4), a rule of the DISABLE statement, which asks the MCS 'to inhibit data transfer between specified output queues and destinations' (§1985:XIV.3.2.1). 2023 has no DISABLE statement, no communication description (CD), no queue and no source: a search of specs/ISO_COBOL_2023.md finds none of 'DISABLE statement', 'cd-name', 'SYMBOLIC SOURCE'. Its MCS is a different facility, an 'implementor-defined system that sends and receives messages exchanged between run units' (§2023:3.118), reached only by SEND and RECEIVE ('The RECEIVE statement receives a message from a requestor or a message server run unit', §2023:14.9.31.1); neither deactivates a logical path. The feature is dropped and no 2023 rule states the requirement.
